form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

Programmes: B.Tech. CSE
Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

AI coding tools/APIs, software development environments, and TA support.
form.12. ASSESSMENT PREFERENCES:
Preferred components: Practical assignments, hands-on coding exercises,
project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

existence.reason: While CSE701 covers aspects of AI in Software Engineering such as data mining and assisting code review, the new course focuses specifically on modern AI-native development, coding agents, MCP, loop engineering, and human-AI collaborative workflows.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course, serving as an applied, workflow-oriented complement to CSE701.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 approaches software engineering through data mining, bug prediction, and research perspectives, whereas the new course focuses on operationalizing AI coding agents, workflow patterns, and context engineering in practical development.

CSE594A emphasizes agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, whereas the new course focuses specifically on software development workflows, tool use (MCP), and software engineering practices.
CSE582 covers product line engineering, maintenance, and legacy systems, whereas the new course examines modern AI-native development and software factories driven by coding agents.
CSE581 covers traditional and agile requirements engineering and design theory, whereas the new course focuses on spec-driven development and executable specifications using AI tools.
AI501 is a core machine learning theory and methodology course, whereas the new course applies engineering practices and evaluation specifically to AI-assisted software development workflows.
CSE201 provides foundational object-oriented programming and unit testing, whereas the new course focuses on automated testing and reliability in AI-native development environments.

prerequisites.justification: Students must understand structured software development, unit testing, and programming principles before building software systems with AI coding agents.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Designed for third and fourth-year Bachelor of Technology students, the course matters because it equips future software engineers with practical capabilities to build and evaluate agent-assisted systems. Upon completing the course, students will be able to implement developer workflows integrating AI-assisted coding tools and coding agents, configure agent skills and Model Context Protocol servers, construct executable specifications, analyze loop engineering and iterative development processes, and evaluate automated testing and reliability metrics. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions, emphasizing a workflow-oriented understanding through hands-on development and experimentation.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress logically from foundational AI-native development workflows and Model Context Protocol mechanisms to specification-driven development, loop engineering, and final reliability evaluation. This ensures students master basic agent interaction before engaging in complex software factories, relying on foundational concepts from prerequisite coursework such as CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix—comprising quizzes, assignments, labs, a midsem exam, a project, and an endsem exam—balances theoretical understanding with practical application. This design fits the course outcomes by directly evaluating students' hands-on ability to configure coding agents, build executable specifications, and deploy automated testing harnesses.
narrative.positioning_rationale: The course differs from CSE701, which focuses on data mining and bug prediction, and CSE594A, which emphasizes algorithmic problem solving, by specifically targeting operationalized AI coding workflows, tool use, and software engineering practices. It also extends foundational software engineering covered in CSE201 into AI-native environments.
